title: Haiku Anagram Generation Using AI: Synthesising Poetic Isomers Through Metaphor-Driven Prompt Engineering (Educational Transformation 002)
abstract: Description (English) Overview This paper presents a novel approach to Japanese haiku anagram generation by extending a three-fold metaphorical framework—quantum mechanics, crystal-growth theory, and organic chemistry—to guide large language models (LLMs) in generating semantically independent new haikus from the identical 17 syllables (morae) of existing haikus. Key Findings: 1. Isomorphic Generation Success: We successfully demonstrate the generation of semantically and aesthetically independent alternative haikus from identical molecular formulae (17-syllable inventories), treating haiku syllables as organic isomers—compounds with identical atomic composition but radically different properties and meanings. 2. Discovery of Poetic Steganography: Haiku anagrams uniquely exhibit a "dual-plaintext structure," where both the original and generated haikus function as independently meaningful poems. This property—unknown in classical anagram theory—constitutes a new form of poetic steganography with high plausible deniability. 3. Metaphor-Driven Cognitive Amplification: By deliberately invoking organic chemistry terminology (structural isomers, enantiomers, racemic mixtures) in prompt design, we observe a quantifiable improvement in token efficiency and aesthetic coherence, demonstrating that humanistic metaphors can systematically redirect LLM outputs toward higher-order creative goals without algorithmic modification. Background & Context The author is a molecular biologist (specialising in RNA) developing liberal arts curricula for first-year undergraduates at the University of Tokyo. This research emerged not from AI expertise but from classroom practice—a workshop inspired by physicist Terahiko Terada's 1922 essay "Chawan no Yu" (A Lesson from a Tea Cup), which advocates connecting scientific and humanistic knowledge through metaphor. Previous work (Educational Transformation 001) applied quantum and crystallisation metaphors to English anagrams with success. However, when adapted to Japanese haikus, the dual-metaphor framework proved insufficient to capture haiku-specific constraints (5-7-5 syllable structure, kire or caesura, yohaku or poetic silence, seasonal reference). The addition of organic chemistry isomerism as a third metaphor resolved these limitations entirely. Methodological Innovation We introduce: - Three-tiered metaphor protocol: Quantum superposition (possibility-space management) → Crystal nucleation (hierarchical structure-building) → Isomeric transformation (semantic distance calibration) - Two-stage synthesis strategy: Molecular-level (preserving ligatures like chiyo as single morae) and thermal decomposition (atomic-level when molecular synthesis reaches impasse) - Five-axis aesthetic evaluation: Meaningfulness (0.30), kire (0.20), yohaku (0.20), tension with original (0.15), defamiliarisation (0.15) - Isomer taxonomy for poetry: 11 isomer-type classifications mapping to increasingly distant poetic transformations (from renzoku isomer to meso-structure) Practical Outcomes From a pedagogical standpoint, this framework enables students (regardless of domain expertise) to experience how metaphor functions as a cognitive technology—not merely literary decoration but a systematic tool for amplifying AI reasoning capacity. The protocol is fully reproducible and available as a prompt template compatible with any LLM. Broader Significance This work occupies the intersection of three disciplines: 1. Constrained literature (Oulipo aesthetics): How AI pursues poetic freedom within human-designed, absolute constraints (17 syllables) 2. Computational creativity: Using AI as a "mirror" that visualises the structure of human aesthetic intuition, rather than as an automated content generator 3. Prompt engineering as humanistic practice: Demonstrating that aesthetic goals can be achieved through metaphorical framing rather than technical modification 概要(日本語) 【授業実践】俳句をアナグラム処理して新しい俳句を作る生成AIワーク 西洋還元主義と美的感覚の協奏:Educational Transformation 002 要旨 本論は、既存の俳句の17音(モーラ)から、同一の音素組成を持ちながら意味として完全に独立した別の俳句を生成するために、量子力学・結晶成長論・有機化学という三重メタファーを大規模言語モデル(LLM)に適用するアプローチを提示する。 主要な発見: 1. 異性体としての句生成の成功:同一の分子式(17音の音素インベントリ)から、意味的・美的に独立した別句の生成に成功。俳句の音は「有機化学の異性体」と見立てることで、同一の原子組成を持ちながら全く異なる性質を示す化合物の概念を詩的に適用した。 2. 詩的ステガノグラフィの発見:俳句アナグラムは「二重平文構造」を持ち、元句も生成句も共に詩として完全に自立するという特性を示す。古典的なアナグラム理論では見られない現象で、「否認可能性」の極めて高い新しい詩的ステガノグラフィ形式を構成する。 3. メタファー駆動型認知増幅:有機化学用語(構造異性体、エナンチオマー、ラセミ体など)をプロンプトに明示的に導入することで、トークン消費量の劇的な改善と美的一貫性の向上を観察。アルゴリズム修正なしに、人文学的メタファーのみがLLMの創造的出力を高次目標へと体系的に誘導できることを実証した。 背景と文脈 著者は東京大学で教養教育の教材開発に携わる分子生物学(RNA専門)の教員であり、本研究はAI専門知ではなく授業実践から生まれた。物理学者・寺田寅彦の随筆「茶わんの湯」(1922)—科学と人文知をメタファーで繋ぐことを主張する古典的論考—を題材にした教養サロンのワークショップが起源である。 前稿(Educational Transformation 001)では量子力学メタファーと結晶成長論メタファーを英語アナグラムに適用して成功を収めた。しかし日本語俳句へ応用する際、この二重メタファーでは5-7-5という音数構造、「切れ」の機能、「余白」の価値、季語の扱いといった俳句固有の詩的制約を十分に捉えられないことが判明。有機化学の「異性体」概念を第三のメタファーとして追加することで、これら三点すべてが劇的に改善された。 方法論の革新性 本研究は以下を導入する: - 三層メタファー・プロトコル:量子的重ね合わせ(可能性空間の管理)→ 結晶核形成(階層的構造構築)→ 異性体化学変換(意味的距離の精密制御) - 二段階合成戦略:分子レベル(拗音を保持)と熱分解レベル(原子まで還元)のフォールバック型アプローチ - 五軸評価関数:意味性(0.30)、切れ(0.20)、余白(0.20)、元句との張力(0.15)、異化効果(0.15) - 詩的異性体分類法:11種類の異性体タイプで元句からの詩的距離を精密に規定(配座異性体から対称メソ体まで) 実践的成果 教育的には、本フレームワークは、メタファーを単なる文学的修辞ではなく「認知技術」として体験する場を提供する。プロトコルは完全に再現可能で、任意のLLMで使用可能なプロンプト・テンプレートとして公開されている。 学際的位置づけ 本取り組みは三つの領域の境界線上に位置する: 1. 制約文学(Oulipo的美学):人間が設計した絶対制約(17音)の中で、AIが詩的自由を追求する新たな人間-AI協働モデル 2. 計算創意学:AIを「自動生成ツール」ではなく、人間の美的直感の構造を可視化する「鏡」として利用 3. 人文主義的プロンプトエンジニアリング:美的目標が技術的修正ではなく、メタファーの枠組みのみで達成可能であることを実証 Keywords / キーワード English: Haiku anagrams, anagram generation, large language models, prompt engineering, metaphor, computational creativity, constrained literature, poetic steganography, organic chemistry isomerism, aesthetic evaluation 日本語: 俳句アナグラム、アナグラム生成、大規模言語モデル、プロンプトエンジニアリング、メタファー、計算創意学、制約文学、詩的ステガノグラフィ、有機化学異性体、美的評価 Disclosure of AI Use / AI使用に関する開示 This document and the research described herein were developed through collaborative dialogue with multiple generative AI systems: 日本語原文の校正: Gemini、ChatGPT、Claude英語版の翻訳・作成: Claude(Sonnet 4.6)英語版の校正: Gemini、ChatGPT俳句異性体解析の実行: Claude(Sonnet 4.6)、Gemini 3 Proプロンプト設計の協議: ChatGPT、Claude、Gemini背景・参考論文: Gemini Deep Research The "Haiku Anagram Isomerism Protocol" (v2.0) described in this work was iteratively refined through multi-turn prompting with Claude. All haiku generation examples and their aesthetic evaluations were executed using Claude Sonnet 4.6, with validation by Gemini 3 Pro. Compliance Note: This disclosure transparently documents AI involvement in accordance with emerging standards for responsible AI research communication. The human researcher (author) remains responsible for all intellectual claims, methodological decisions, and educational outcomes. title: K4Sekolah: School Context Data Files for TIMSS 2023 Grade 4
abstract: The official TIMSS 2023 website provides the School Context Data Files for TIMSS 2023 Grade 4 in rdata format. However, the available data are presented solely in the form of numerical values. This package aims to transform the numerical data into categorical data, thereby enabling clearer interpretation and reducing ambiguity in statistical data analysis. Furthermore, the category labels are presented in Bahasa Indonesia. This initiative is intended as a contribution to promoting and expanding the use of Bahasa Indonesia in the field of programming, in line with its designation as one of the official languages of the United Nations General Assembly.

title: Dynamic Learning in the Spatio-Temporal Continuum
abstract: While AI-driven clinical workflows in medical imaging offer significant potential for patient safety, model robustness and generalization are frequently hindered by the static world assumption of current AI models. In practice, this domain is highly dynamic, with distributions shifting significantly across both location (spatial) and time (temporal). For example, artifacts or changes in patient populations are inherent to medical imaging and manifest across both dimensions. Such diverse training data is usually not available from only one hospital or point in time. Since privacy regulations restrict the sharing of patient data between hospitals and its long-term storage, spatio-temporally distributed training is crucial to bridge the spatio-temporal data availability gap. Federated Learning and Continual Learning are well-established concepts to address these gaps. However, in the dynamic clinical reality, they suffer from performance degradation: Federated Learning is affected by Client Drift when data distributions differ spatially, while Continual Learning suffers from Catastrophic Forgetting when distributions shift over time. Existing methods address these separately or require prior knowledge of the underlying distribution changes. Consequently, existing research neglects the potential of a more dynamic joint method to robustly overcome data availability challenges in dynamic clinical environments. In the first part of this work, we empirically demonstrate a strong correlation between performance degradation caused by shifts in both dimensions, motivating the introduction of a new paradigm for robust spatio-temporally distributed training termed Dynamic Learning. We propose DynBC, a Dynamic Learning method that significantly outperforms existing conventional state-of-the-art approaches. Beyond the dynamic nature of medical imaging, the deployment of dynamic spatio-temporally distributed training to overcome the data availability gap is also hindered by rigid medical device regulations that fail to acknowledge the dynamic reality of medical imaging. We analyze the Predetermined Change Control Plan as a novel regulatory framework proposed by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration that is the first of its kind to address this issue from a regulatory perspective. We identify three critical gaps and propose solutions to each of them to fully enable the legal clinical deployment of dynamic models. Deploying spatio-temporally distributed training in real-world clinical settings is the last major challenge for our holistic approach to overcome the problem of data availability. Consequently, in this work, we present the first deployment of Federated Learning for histopathology segmentation of colorectal cancer tissue within the infrastructure of German university hospitals. In a nationwide project, we demonstrate the ability of our framework to train on data that is distributed across a geographic area of 10,500 km². By addressing these challenges, our work helps to bring these dynamic models closer to clinical reality. We bridge the gap between achieving robust training under spatio-temporal distribution shifts, regulatory adaptation, and translation into clinical applications, thereby improving clinical workflows and patient safety.

title: Shielding Federated Learning Services From a Novel Stealthy Label-Flipping Attack Exposing Membership
abstract: Label-flipping attacks pose a significant threat to the security and privacy of machine learning models, particularly in federated learning (FL). While existing defenses, such as FoolsGold and Krum, aim to mitigate these attacks, they often fail to account for more subtle adversarial behaviors, such as intermittent class-targeted flips. In this work, we introduce theStealthy Label-Flipping Attack (SLFA), which exposes this overlooked vulnerability in FL services. SLFA is an adaptive attack that intermittently flips a fixed subset of class labels across multiple communication rounds before reverting them to their original state. We show that this transient manipulation (i) evades state-of-the-art poisoning and anomaly detectors, (ii) preserves overall model utility, and (iii) introduces gradient instability during the attacking rounds, thereby increasing the risk of privacy leakage. To counter this hybrid threat that not only evades state-of-the-art defenses but also amplifies privacy leakage, we proposeFLStealthShield, a server-side defense mechanism that detects and neutralizes such adaptive attacks by analyzing temporal patterns in client updates. Extensive experiments under both IID and non-IID data distributions demonstrate that FLStealthShield achieves Byzantine robustness and maintains high model utility, outperforming existing defenses even when over 40% of clients are malicious.

title: High-Speed Real-Time Random Bit Generation Based on a Modeless Raman Fiber Laser
abstract: True random numbers are essential for cryptography and secure communications. Algorithmically generated pseudo-random numbers lack true physical randomness, while conventional lasers as physical entropy sources introduce time-delay signatures (TDS) and require complex post processing. To address this challenge, this study presents a high speed, real-time true random bit generator utilizing a modeless Raman fiber laser (RFL). A modeless RFL was constructed using an ultra-low reflectivity (-27 dB) fiber Bragg grating (FBG) and a high-reflectivity FBG serving as cavity mirrors. The laser delivers stable modeless Raman lasing within the pump power range of 5 W to 10 W. Compared with multilongitudinal-mode operation, the modeless laser exhibits significantly lower temporal coherence. By truncating the four least significant bits of the 8-bit digitized temporal intensity signal from the modeless RFL, random bit sequences were generated at a rate of 320 Gbps. The resulting random bit stream shows a uniform distribution of bits 0 and 1, its autocorrelation function contains no TDS, and it successfully passes the NIST statistical test. In contrast, the same generation method fails to produce qualified random bits when applied to the Raman fiber laser operating in the multilongitudinal-mode regime. The demonstrated modeless RFL system combines real-time operation, high speed, and stability, offering a robust physical entropy source for cryptographic and secure communication applications.

title: Doctor Patient Summarizer: Transformer-based Patient-Friendly Medical Summaries
abstract: The conversations between patients and doctors include vital clinical data that should be properly recorded to enable effective clinical decision-making and patient comprehension. These interactions cannot be summarized in a manual manner that is both time-consuming and may cause inconsistencies, omissions and fatigue in documentation. Despite the recent advances in transformer-based natural language processing (NLP) models, which have enhanced automated clinical summarization models, a large number of the currently existing models have difficulties with the long conversational context and frequently give patients summaries that are hard to understand because of highly technical language. The present paper presents a proposal of a transformer-based system based on the Vision Transformer (ViT) architecture to produce concise, medically accurate and patient-friendly summaries of clinical conversations. The given strategy splits the dialogue tokens into regular semantic patches, which allows to generate a long context modeling efficiently and retain conversational coherence. The preprocessing pipeline including the speaker identification, medical terms normalization and the contextual filtering is added to enhance the factual consistency, and less ambiguity in the summaries generated. The model is trained on selected curated clinical dialogues datasets and compared with the standard summarization baselines with the help of classic metrics, such as ROUGE, BERT Score, and medical specificity accuracy indicators. Results of the experiment indicate that there is better summary coherence, factual preservation and readability than conventional transformer-based architectures. Also, attention-based interpretability indicates clinically significance of dialogue segments that are relevant towards the summary generation process. The suggested framework does not only lead to better clinical documentation efficiency and communication between the healthcare providers and the patients, but also aids in a safer and more transparent arrival of health care information.

title: Global Context-Aware Multi-Instance Learning for Whole Slide Image Classification
abstract: Multi-instance learning (MIL) is an effective weakly supervised learning paradigm where each sample is a bag of unlabeled instances, making it particularly suitable for whole slide image (WSI) classification, as WSIs can reach gigapixel resolutions, with supervision available only at the bag (WSI) level. However, WSIs often suffer from spurious correlations and an overwhelming number of negative instances, leading to underutilization of key instances. To address these issues, we propose the global context-aware multi-instance learning with asymmetric contrast (GCA-MIL) algorithm with two key strategies. The global context-aware (GCA) strategy consists of a class token, a global context, and a key instance, designed to extract and transfer contextual knowledge. Building on this, the asymmetric contrast strategy incorporates a triplet loss to strengthen the similarity between the global context and the key instance while reducing the association with negative anchor instances. Experiments on the CAMELYON16 dataset show that GCA-MIL outperforms state-of-the-art MIL approaches.

title: QCA-RAG: Efficient Retrieval for LLMs via Query Complexity Awareness
abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) has become a key paradigm for enhancing the knowledge and reasoning capabilities of large language models (LLMs). However, conventional approaches treat all queries uniformly, leading to unnecessary retrieval cost and suboptimal performance for queries of varying complexity. To adress thie issue, we propose QCA-RAG, a Query Complexity-Aware framework that dynamically adjusts retrieval behavior based on query complexity, enabling the LLM to generate high-quality responses with reduced retrieval overhead. Experiments on four datasets covering diverse query complexities show that QCA-RAG improves answer quality while reducing retrieval latency compared to both fixed and adaptive baselines, demonstrating its effectiveness in balancing efficiency and accuracy across factoid and multi-hop QA tasks.

title: Hybrid Continuous Variable Quantum Neural Network for Audio Classification
abstract: Audio classification is a key application in deep learning, and quantum machine learning (QML) provides new possibilities by capturing complex patterns in signals through parameterized quantum circuits. However, existing qubit-based models struggle to efficiently represent continuous-valued data common in audio processing, limiting their scalability and expressivity. Continuous Variable Quantum Computing (CVQC) offers a natural framework for processing real-valued data such as mel-spectrograms, addressing the limitations of qubit-based systems while introducing nonlinearity through non-gaussian gates to ensure universality. In CVQC, each qumode represents an infinite-dimensional Hilbert space, enabling compact yet expressive information representation. This work introduces a two-qumode Hybrid Continuous Variable Quantum Neural Network (HCVQNN) for audio classification that integrates classical neural layers with a CV quantum circuit for advanced feature extraction and encoding. Experiments conducted using PennyLane demonstrate that HCVQNN achieves comparable audio classification accuracy while requiring fewer resources compared to classical deep networks and qubit-based quantum models.

title: Ara-BEST-RQ: Multi Dialectal Arabic SSL
abstract: We present Ara-BEST-RQ, a family of self-supervised learning (SSL) models specifically designed for multi-dialectal Arabic speech processing. Leveraging 5,640 hours of crawled Creative Commons speech and combining it with publicly available datasets, we pre-train conformer-based BEST-RQ models up to 600M parameters. Our models are evaluated on dialect identification (DID) and automatic speech recognition (ASR) tasks, achieving state-of-the-art performance on the former while using fewer parameters than competing models. We demonstrate that family-targeted pre-training on Arabic dialects significantly improves downstream performance compared to multilingual or monolingual models trained on non-Arabic data. All models, code, and pre-processed datasets will be publicly released to support reproducibility and further research in Arabic speech technologies.

title: AngularDINO: Semi-Supervised Anomaly Detection via Self-Distillation with Hybrid Angular Margin
abstract: Anomaly detection often suffers when training data assumed to be normal are contaminated with anomalies, causing severe performance degradation. Semi-supervised approaches attempt to leverage a few labeled anomalies, but they remain fragile to contamination and can even perform worse than unsupervised methods. To address this issue, we propose AngularDINO, a novel self-distillation framework that incorporates a key mechanism, called the hybrid angular margin. This mechanism applies complementary margins to the student and teacher networks: an additive margin encourages the student to form a discriminative feature space, while a subtractive margin ensures the teacher provides stable supervision. Through this design, AngularDINO enables robust anomaly detection even with limited labeled data. Experiments on standard benchmarks demonstrate that AngularDINO achieves significant performance gains over previous unsupervised and semi-supervised methods under contaminated scenarios.

title: QPath: A Question-Aware Multi-Resolution Vision Language Framework for Computational Pathology
abstract: Computational pathology has recently advanced through the use of multimodal large language models (MLLMs) for visual question answering (VQA). However, most existing approaches rely on single-resolution analysis of pathology images, limiting their ability to capture both global and fine-grained morphological cues. In this work, we introduce QPath, a novel MLLM that integrates multi-resolution analysis via question-aware patch retrieval. For region-of-interest (ROI) images, QPath crops them into patches and fuses the top-k question-relevant patches with the original view to enhance localized reasoning. For whole-slide images (WSIs), we propose a dynamic sampling strategy that balances spatial coverage with semantic relevance, enabling efficient yet comprehensive slide-level understanding. Extensive experiments show that QPath achieves state-of-the-art performance on ROI-level VQA benchmarks and exhibits strong zero-shot generalization to WSI-level tasks.

title: Improving Automatic Speech Recognition by Mitigating Distortions Introduced by Speech Enhancement Under Drone Noise
abstract: This paper proposes a method to improve automatic speech recognition (ASR) performance against drone noise-contaminated audio recordings by mitigating distortions resulted from speech enhancement (SE). Our system combines a front-end Adaptive Fusion Model (AFM) with a back-end Biasing Network (BN). The AFM, serving as the core of our proposed fusion-based method, adaptively fuses intermediate outputs from a diffusion-based SE model to optimize the noise-distortion trade-off, while the BN mitigates acoustic mismatch by correcting speech features using static noise characteristics, thereby avoiding costly ASR retraining. Experimental results with three types of drone noise across multiple signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) levels (0, -5, and -10 dB) demonstrated the robustness of the proposed system. In particular, for SNRs of -5 dB and above, the method consistently showed clear effectiveness, yielding about 20- and 25-point absolute character error rate (CER) improvements at 0 and -5 dB, respectively, compared to an ASR-only baseline.

title: Role-Specialist and Confidence-Selective Multi-Teacher Collaborative Distillation for Multi-Source Domain Adaptation
abstract: Multi-source domain adaptation is hampered by compounded inter-domain gaps and scarce target labels, making it hard for a single model to disentangle invariant from specific features. To address this, we propose a multi-teacher collaborative distillation framework that assigns distinct roles to different teachers: multi-source teachers focus on distilling robust domain-invariant knowledge, while a target-domain teacher leverages the collective wisdom of the source teachers to generate reliable pseudo-labels and capture the unique distribution of the target domain. These teachers interact via mutual distillation to dynamically integrate domain-invariant and domain-specific knowledge. Further, to meet resource constraints, a lightweight student model is introduced, which first absorbs global knowledge via standard distillation and then refines high-confidence target samples through disentangled knowledge distillation. This yields representations that are both generalizable and precise. Extensive experiments on standard image classification benchmarks demonstrate significant improvements over existing methods.

title: Optimized cross-attention GRU-transformer network with sooty tern algorithm for accurate solar power forecasting
abstract: Accurate forecasting of solar Photovoltaic (PV) power remains challenging due to data uncertainty, environmental fluctuations, and missing sensor values. To address these issues, this study introduces, an integrated deep learning and optimization framework designed for real-time PV power prediction. The approach begins with a rigorous data preprocessing pipeline that incorporates a hybrid imputation strategy combining Simple Imputer for categorical gaps and K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) imputer for numerical inconsistencies. Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA) and time-series decomposition further enhance the temporal interpretability of the dataset, while engineered feature transformations provide more informative inputs. The proposed hybrid STO-CrossEchoTransGRUNet model fuses the strengths of an Echo State Network (ESN) for global temporal encoding, a cross-attention transformer (CATL) for modelling multi-feature interactions and a Bidirectional GRU for capturing long-term bidirectional dependencies. To further boost performance, hyperparameters are optimized using Sooty Tern Optimization (STO) with a Levy flight–based spiral foraging mechanism. Benchmarking against traditional machine learning models and contemporary deep learning architectures demonstrates the superior accuracy, robustness and computational efficiency of the proposed method. Experimental evaluation validates significant improvements, achieving aRoot Mean Square Error (RMSE) of 0.015, Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 0.005, Median Absolute Error (MedAE) of 0.002, R² of 0.995 and consistently stable performance across varying environmental conditions. These results highlight STO-CrossEchoTransGRUNet as a highly reliable and scalable solution for real-time solar PV forecasting.

title: Generative Drifting for Conditional Medical Image Generation
abstract: Conditional medical image generation plays an important role in many clinically relevant imaging tasks. However, existing methods still face a fundamental challenge in balancing inference efficiency, patient-specific fidelity, and distribution-level plausibility, particularly in high-dimensional 3D medical imaging. In this work, we propose GDM, a generative drifting framework that reformulates deterministic medical image prediction as a multi-objective learning problem to jointly promote distribution-level plausibility and patient-specific fidelity while retaining one-step inference. GDM extends drifting to 3D medical imaging through an attractive-repulsive drift that minimizes the discrepancy between the generator pushforward and the target distribution. To enable stable drifting-based learning in 3D volumetric data, GDM constructs a multi-level feature bank from a medical foundation encoder to support reliable affinity estimation and drifting field computation across complementary global, local, and spatial representations. In addition, a gradient coordination strategy in the shared output space improves optimization balance under competing distribution-level and fidelity-oriented objectives. We evaluate the proposed framework on two representative tasks, MRI-to-CT synthesis and sparse-view CT reconstruction. Experimental results show that GDM consistently outperforms a wide range of baselines, including GAN-based, flow-matching-based, and SDE-based generative models, as well as supervised regression methods, while improving the balance among anatomical fidelity, quantitative reliability, perceptual realism, and inference efficiency. These findings suggest that GDM provides a practical and effective framework for conditional 3D medical image generation.

title: ISSE: An Instruction-Guided Speech Style Editing Dataset and Benchmark
abstract: Speech style editing refers to modifying the stylistic properties of speech while preserving its linguistic content and speaker identity. However, most existing approaches depend on explicit labels or reference audio, which limits both flexibility and scalability. More recent attempts to use natural language descriptions remain constrained by oversimplified instructions and coarse style control. To address these limitations, we introduce an Instruction-guided Speech Style Editing Dataset (ISSE). The dataset comprises nearly 400 hours of speech and over 100,000 source-target pairs, each aligned with diverse and detailed textual editing instructions. We also build a systematic instructed speech data generation pipeline leveraging large language model, expressive text-to-speech and voice conversion technologies to construct high-quality paired samples. Furthermore, we train an instruction-guided autoregressive speech model on ISSE and evaluate it in terms of instruction adherence, timbre preservation, and content consistency. Experimental results demonstrate that ISSE enables accurate, controllable, and generalizable speech style editing compared to other datasets. The project page of ISSE is available at https://ychenn1.github.io/ISSE/.

title: RetrieveAll: A Multilingual Named Entity Recognition Framework with Large Language Models
abstract: The rise of large language models has led to breakthroughs in named entity recognition for high-resource languages, yet substantial room for improvement remains in low- and medium-resource languages. Existing multilingual named entity recognition methods face severe language interference during the multi-language adaptation process, manifested in feature conflicts between different languages and the competitive suppression of low-resource language features by high-resource languages. Although training a dedicated model for each language can mitigate such interference, it lacks scalability and incurs excessive computational costs in real-world applications. To address this issue, we propose RetrieveAll, a universal multilingual named entity recognition framework based on dynamic LoRA. The framework decouples task-specific features across languages and demonstrates efficient dynamic adaptability. Furthermore, we introduce a cross-granularity knowledge augmented method that fully exploits the intrinsic potential of the data without relying on external resources. Experimental results show that RetrieveAll achieves an average F1 improvement of 12.1% on the PAN-X dataset.

title: TestAgent: Automatic Benchmarking and Exploratory Interaction for Evaluating LLMS in Vertical Domains
abstract: As Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed in highly specialized vertical domains, the evaluation of their domain-specific performance becomes critical. However, existing evaluations for vertical domains typically rely on the labor-intensive construction of static single-turn datasets, which present two key limitations: (i) manual data construction is costly and must be repeated for each new domain, and (ii) static single-turn evaluations are misaligned with the dynamic multi-turn interactions in real-world applications, limiting the assessment of professionalism and stability. To address these, we propose TestAgent, a framework for automatic benchmarking and exploratory dynamic evaluation in vertical domains. TestAgent leverages retrieval-augmented generation to create domain-specific questions from user-provided knowledge sources, combined with a two-stage criteria generation process, thereby enabling scalable and automated benchmark creation. Furthermore, it introduces a reinforcement learning-guided multi-turn interaction strategy that adaptively determines question types based on real-time model responses, dynamically probing knowledge boundaries and stability. Extensive experiments across medical, legal, and governmental domains demonstrate that TestAgent enables efficient cross-domain benchmark generation and yields deeper insights into model behavior through dynamic exploratory evaluation. This work establishes a new paradigm for automated and in-depth evaluation of LLMs in vertical domains.

title: Integrating AI to Improve Customer Experience and Marketing in Zambia’s Insurance Sector: A Case Study of Selected Insurance Firms
abstract: The rapid evolution of digital technologies has significantly transformed service delivery and customer engagement in the global insurance industry. Artificial Intelligence (AI) plays a central role in this transformation by enhancing operational efficiency, personalizing customer interactions, and improving marketing strategies. However, the adoption and impact of AI in Zambia’s insurance sector remain limited and underexplored. This study investigates the integration of AI to improve customer experience and marketing effectiveness in selected Zambian insurance firms using a mixed-methods approach. Quantitative data from 100 respondents revealed that 63% reported some use of AI systems, while only 31% confirmed the presence of AI chatbots. Mean scores for AI usage and marketing effectiveness were 3.21 and 3.22, with a moderate positive correlation (r = 0.566, p < 0.01). Qualitative findings from 25 interviews highlighted key themes, including limited enterprise-level adoption, operational efficiency gains, improved customer targeting, and reliance on hybrid service models. Barriers such as skills gaps, data limitations, and unclear regulations persist. The study concludes that while AI offers significant opportunities, its full potential depends on strategic implementation, capacity building, and regulatory support within Zambia’s insurance sector.

title: Enhancing Arabic NLP
abstract: Arabic is a first language for more than 300 million people. It has some unique features that can make it one of the most complex languages, such as multiple derivatives, unlimited vocabulary, diacritics, and others. Preprocessing Arabic text is an essential step in order to prepare text for Natural Language Processing (NLP) purposes. This article provides a comparison study of several preprocessing tools for Arabic text. It explains the challenges in pre-processing the Arabic language as well as the techniques that used in every particular tool. However, the authors used the PRISMA for reporting the systematic reviews, which they started with screening 200 articles and ended-up with including only 30 articles. After reviewing these articles deeply, the results show that different tools such as AMIRA, CAMel ,and NLP packages added value in text-preprocessing. However, most of this papers considered that the ambiguity in Arabic orthography as well as the dialectal variants are the most challenges in Arabic NLP.

title: Multimodal Deep Learning-based Precision Treatment for Lung Cancer
abstract: Early and accurate classification of lung cancer is important in the development of an effective treatment plan and the achievement of high survival rates. This paper presents the development of a multimodal deep learning framework for the classification of lung cancer based on the use of computed tomography imaging and clinical data. ROI images of the tumor-focused CT scans are used in the imaging analysis process. The clinical features were preprocessed using encoding and normalization, while fully connected neural networks were used in the modeling process. Feature-level fusion is also used in the study, which is done by concatenating the features in the proposed framework. Five-fold cross-validation is used in the study. Pre-trained convolutional neural networks, including VGG16, ResNet50, DenseNet121, and EfficientNetB0, were used in the study to explore the use of the networks in the automated feature extraction process from the CT scans. The proposed model shows better performance compared to other existing techniques.

title: DSG: Dual-Semantic Guidance from LLM to Token Distillation for Few-Shot Incremental Learning
abstract: Few-shot class-incremental learning (FSCIL) must acquire new classes from limited data while preserving prior knowledge, where overfitting and catastrophic forgetting remain key challenges. Prior work typically relies on a single semantic cue, such as class names or descriptions, to complement visual features. We propose DSG, a dual-semantic guidance framework that distills complementary textual semantics into the ViT language branch without modifying the visual backbone: (i) TLTA, a template-driven low-rank text adapter that maps fixed-format class names to a session-stable semantic anchor; and (ii) DG-TSA, a description-guided, temperature-scaled attention that aggregates attribute-grouped descriptions into a dynamic semantic prototype. Together, DSG provides stable anchors to suppress semantic drift and adaptive fine-grained cues beyond static prompts, improving novel-class adaptation while retaining old knowledge. Experiments on CUB-200, miniImageNet, and CIFAR-100 demonstrate consistent gains over strong baselines. Code is available at: https://github.com/BUCT-IUSRC/Research__DSG.

title: Adaptive Defense Against Stationary Test-Time Attacks on Classifiers
abstract: In many classification tasks performed by autonomous systems, a classifier model is continuously used to compute decisions for a series of incoming test examples. In such scenarios, a test-time attack may falsify a series of test examples to continuously perturb the classification decisions of the system. Under the assumption of time-invariant but unknown attack mapping, we propose a novel adaptive defense approach consisting of two main components: an attack-type detector that identifies the nature of the ongoing attack from a small batch of attacked examples, and a set of specialized expert classifiers, each adversarially trained to be robust against a specific attack type. At test-time, the detector routes the input batch to the appropriate expert classifier. We demonstrate through experiments on the CIFAR-10 dataset that our adaptive defense significantly outperforms static defense approaches, highlighting the benefits of adapting the classifier model by leveraging the inferred characteristics of the ongoing attack.

title: DynaPredict: Alternating Predictive and Real Iteration for Efficient Deep Reinforcement Learning Training
abstract: Sample-inefficient in Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) impedes scalability and practical deployment. While model-based Reinforcement Learning (MBRL) improves efficiency through environmental simulation, it suffers from model bias and high computational costs. Conversely, conventional optimizers adapt poorly to DRL’s non-stationary optimization landscapes. To bridge this gap, we introduce DynaPredict, a novel optimization framework that transposes the concept of environmental simulation from observation space to parameter space. Instead of predicting observations, DynaPredict employs a lightweight predictive component to forecast the trajectory of policy parameter updates, thereby implicitly encoding environmental feedback. Our method alternates between predictive and real update cycles, drastically reducing environment interactions while avoiding model bias. Empirically, DynaPredict achieves consistent performance gains across the Atari benchmark, reducing sample complexity by up to 60% and accelerating wall-clock convergence time, demonstrating benefits orthogonal to specific algorithms or parallel architectures.

title: TAML: Task-Aware Metric-Driven Meta Learning for Few-Shot Action Recognition
abstract: Recent few-shot action recognition (FSAR) methods often adopt pre-trained visual backbones with temporal alignment modules for metric-based classification. However, directly fine-tuning large models or inserting lightweight adapters without explicit guidance fails to emphasize task-relevant metric representations. With limited samples and high-capacity backbones, adapting these models to learn transferable metric features remains challenging. To address this, we propose TAML, a task-level meta-learning paradigm that constructs meta-metric tasks to explicitly learn metric-relevant representations and enhance generalization. Our framework integrates task-specific learning, where the model captures metric information for individual tasks, with task-agnostic learning, which optimizes shared meta-features to capture multi-grained matching information. Experiments on standard datasets show that TAML consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods.

evidence.abstract: Recent few-shot action recognition (FSAR) methods often adopt pre-trained visual backbones with temporal alignment modules for metric-based classification. However, directly fine-tuning large models or inserting lightweight adapters without explicit guidance fails to emphasize task-relevant metric representations. With limited samples and high-capacity backbones, adapting these models to learn transferable metric features remains challenging. To address this, we propose TAML, a task-level meta-learning paradigm that constructs meta-metric tasks to explicitly learn metric-relevant representations and enhance generalization. Our framework integrates task-specific learning, where the model captures metric information for individual tasks, with task-agnostic learning, which optimizes shared meta-features to capture multi-grained matching information. Experiments on standard datasets show that TAML consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods.

title: Palette: A Background-Robust Fingerprinting Attack on Air Interface Designed for Cross-Environment Challenges
abstract: Smartphones are indispensable devices in daily life. Due to the openness of the air interface between user equipment (UE) and base station (BS), wireless fingerprint sniffing has emerged as a significant privacy threat. Previous studies have conducted attacks in laboratory environments, assuming no background apps are running on the target UEs. This idealistic assumption diminishes the practicality of air interface fingerprint attacks. In this paper, we propose Palette, a novel fingerprint attack adaptable to various background environments. Specifically, Palette employs a pre-built background traffic library to augment the raw data. Subsequently, Palette utilizes multi-level traffic aggregation to extract robust features from the augmented traffic. Finally, drawing inspiration from speaker recognition, Palette builds a robust classifier based on Time Delay Neural Network (TDNN). Extensive cross-environment experiments demonstrate that Palette outperforms state-of-the-art (SOTA) methods and improves the F1-score for app identification by an average of 28.01% when other background applications are running.

title: Quantum Gasp Codes for Private Distributed Matrix Multiplication
abstract: We develop quantum gap additive secure polynomial (GASP) codes. Classical GASP codes have been designed for the private distributed matrix multiplication (PDMM) problem for outer product partitioning (OPP). In PDMM, a user, with limited computation resources, sends high-dimensional matrices to servers with high computation power to compute the required product such that any T of the servers cannot get any information about the user’s matrices. In the quantum setting, the user sends the encoded versions of the matrices to the servers over classical channels, and the servers respond back over separate quantum channels individually using an encoded share of a pre-established entangled state. In this paper, we define the requirement that the classical code of GASP should satisfy in order for it to be transformed into a quantum code. We develop the encoding structure once the requirement is satisfied, achieving the super-dense coding gain, i.e., double the classical rate counterpart. Finally, we quantify the limitation to satisfy the aforementioned feasibility requirement, i.e., the minimum privacy parameter needed to transform the classical code to its quantum counterpart.

title: Latent Space Orthonormalization for Hyper-Finetuning of Language Models
abstract: The increasing popularity of parameter-efficient finetuning (PEFT) methods has facilitated the efficient adaptation of pre-trained language models (LMs) to new tasks. Recent methods combine low-rank adaptation methods and hypernetworks (HNets) to enhance the performance of PEFT. However, despite their potential, these methods are limited by their representation capacity. To overcome this limitation, we propose a novel framework that incorporates latent space orthonormalization for PEFT using HNets. Our novel HNet architecture generates orthonormal components from a set of learnable parameter representations to effectively estimate the low-rank adaptation parameters. To ensure stability and prevent overfitting, we regularize and constrain the latent space and components during training. The experimental results show that our framework obtains state-of-the-art results on both language understanding and generation tasks. In particular, for language understanding tasks, our framework outperforms the baselines by 3% and 4% on the GLUE and SuperGLUE benchmarks, respectively, without increasing the computation cost during the inference step.

title: Localizing Speech Deepfakes Beyond Transitions via Segment-Aware Learning
abstract: Localizing partial deepfake audio, where only segments of speech are manipulated, remains challenging due to the subtle and scattered nature of these modifications. Existing approaches typically rely on frame-level predictions to identify spoofed segments, and some recent methods improve performance by concentrating on the transitions between real and fake audio. However, we observe that these models tend to over-rely on boundary artifacts while neglecting the manipulated content that follows. We argue that effective localization requires understanding the entire segments beyond just detecting transitions. Thus, we propose Segment-Aware Learning (SAL), a framework that encourages models to focus on the internal structure of segments. SAL introduces two core techniques: Segment Positional Labeling, which provides fine-grained frame supervision based on relative position within a segment; and Cross-Segment Mixing, a data augmentation method that generates diverse segment patterns. Experiments across multiple deepfake localization datasets show that SAL consistently achieves strong performance in both in-domain and out-of-domain settings, with notable gains in non-boundary regions and reduced reliance on transition artifacts. The code is available at https://github.com/SentryMao/SAL.

title: Clustering-Driven Memory Compression for on-Device Large Language Models
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) often rely on user-specific memories distilled from past interactions to enable personalized generation. A common practice is to concatenate these memories with the input prompt, but this approach quickly exhausts the limited context available in on-device LLMs. Compressing memories by averaging can mitigate context growth, yet it frequently harms performance due to semantic conflicts across heterogeneous memories. In this work, we introduce a clustering-based memory compression strategy that balances context efficiency and personalization quality. Our method groups memories by similarity and merges them within clusters prior to concatenation, thereby preserving coherence while reducing redundancy. Experiments demonstrate that our approach substantially lowers the number of memory tokens while outperforming baseline strategies such as naive averaging or direct concatenation. Furthermore, for a fixed context budget, clustering-driven merging yields more compact memory representations and consistently enhances generation quality.

title: SE-DiCoW: Self-Enrolled Diarization-Conditioned Whisper
abstract: Speaker-attributed automatic speech recognition (ASR) in multi-speaker environments remains a major challenge. While some approaches achieve strong performance when fine-tuned on specific domains, few systems generalize well across out-of-domain datasets. Our prior work, Diarization-Conditioned Whisper (DiCoW), leverages speaker diarization outputs as conditioning information and, with minimal fine-tuning, demonstrated strong multilingual and multi-domain performance. In this paper, we address a key limitation of DiCoW: ambiguity in Silence–Target–Non-target–Overlap (STNO) masks, where two or more fully overlapping speakers may have nearly identical conditioning despite differing transcriptions. We introduce SE-DiCoW (Self-Enrolled Diarization-Conditioned Whisper), which uses diarization output to locate an enrollment segment anywhere in the conversation where the target speaker is most active. This enrollment segment is used as fixed conditioning via cross-attention at each encoder layer. We further refine DiCoW with improved data segmentation, model initialization, and augmentation. Together, these advances yield substantial gains: SE-DiCoW reduces macro-averaged tcpWER by 52.4% relative to the original DiCoW on the EMMA MT-ASR benchmark.

title: Multi-Scale Adaptive Neighborhood Awareness Transformer for Graph Fraud Detection
abstract: Graph fraud detection (GFD) is crucial for identifying fraudulent behavior within graphs, benefiting various domains such as financial networks and social media. Existing methods based on graph neural networks (GNNs) have succeeded considerably due to their effective expressive capacity for graph-structured data. However, the inherent inductive bias of GNNs, including the homogeneity assumption and the limited global modeling ability, hinder the effectiveness of these models. To address these challenges, we propose Multi-scale Neighborhood Awareness Transformer (MANDATE), which alleviates the inherent inductive bias of GNNs. Specifically, we design a multi-scale positional encoding strategy to encode the positional information of various distances from the central node. By incorporating it with the self-attention mechanism, the global modeling ability can be enhanced significantly. Meanwhile, we design different embedding strategies for homophilic and heterophilic connections. This mitigates the homophily distribution differences between benign and fraudulent nodes. Moreover, an embedding fusion strategy is designed for multi-relation graphs, which alleviates the distribution bias caused by different relationships. Experiments on three fraud detection datasets demonstrate the superiority of MANDATE.

title: NMGE: Nested Multi-Granularity Expert Groups for Complexity-Aware Routing in Multilingual Translation
abstract: Multilingual Neural Machine Translation (MNMT) suffers from task interference, especially under parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT). While Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) methods can alleviate this problem by specializing experts, they often fail to fully leverage knowledge transfer due to sparse, unsupervised routing. In this work, we propose Nested Multi-Granularity Expert Groups (NMGE), a novel MoE architecture where experts are organized into groups of varying sizes in a nested structure. It ensures shared experts across different inputs to prompt knowledge sharing. We further introduce a supervised routing mechanism that uses training losses to guide token-level expert selection. Experiments on WMT show that NMGE improves translation performance across language directions, outperforming strong baselines in multi-lingual settings.

title: SEARAG: Semantic Entropy-Guided Adaptive Retrieval for Multi-Hop Question Answering
abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) enhances Large Language Models (LLMs) in knowledge-intensive tasks, but static retrieval strategies fail to adapt to evolving informational needs, often yielding insufficient or redundant content. Existing adaptive retrieval methods rely on output probabilities or heuristics, which poorly capture the model’s true knowledge needs. To address this, we propose Semantic Entropy-based Adaptive RAG (SEARAG), which trains a discriminative model to predict binary semantic entropy from hidden-layer states, quantifying uncertainty in real time. During generation, we use iterative sentence-by-sentence reasoning: if high semantic entropy is detected, external knowledge retrieval is triggered; otherwise, the process continues. This mechanism identifies knowledge needs, reduces redundancy, and improves quality. Experiments on five multi-hop QA tasks show SEARAG outperforms existing adaptive RAG methods in both performance and efficiency, demonstrating its effectiveness and generalization.

title: TRACE: Optimizing Multi-Hop Question Answering via Confidence-Guided Retrieval Assimilation
abstract: Complex question answering with multi-hop reasoning typically requires long reasoning chains and leads to high computational costs. Existing approaches often focus on a single aspect: reasoning compression may omit critical information, while retrieval augmentation can lead to excessive expansion, making it difficult to balance efficiency and accuracy. Inspired by human cognition, we propose TRACE, which generates candidate answers at cognitive transfer points and evaluates their confidence. High-confidence answers are directly returned, while low-confidence ones trigger retrieval. Fact units are extracted to identify immediate cognitive needs, and the retrieved information is compared with the historical reasoning chain: conflicting information prompts assimilation, whereas non-conflicting information extends the knowledge chain. This design enables retrieval augmentation under the constraint of non-redundant reasoning, thereby balancing efficiency and accuracy. Experimental results demonstrate that TRACE reduces token consumption on three multi-hop QA datasets while achieving performance comparable to or surpassing state-of-the-art baselines.

title: DMP-TTS: Disentangled Multi-Modal Prompting for Controllable Text-to-Speech with Chained Guidance
abstract: Controllable text-to-speech (TTS) systems face significant challenges in achieving independent manipulation of speaker timbre and speaking style, often suffering from entanglement between these attributes. We present DMP-TTS, a latent Diffusion Transformer (DiT) framework with explicit disentanglement and multi-modal prompting. A CLAP-based style encoder (Style-CLAP) aligns cues from reference audio and descriptive text in a shared space and is trained with contrastive learning plus multi-task supervision on style attributes. For fine-grained control during inference, we introduce chained classifier-free guidance (cCFG) trained with hierarchical condition dropout, enabling independent adjustment of content, timbre, and style guidance strengths. Additionally, we employ Representation Alignment (REPA) to distill acoustic-semantic features from a pretrained Whisper model into intermediate DiT representations, stabilizing training and accelerating convergence. Experiments show that DMP-TTS delivers stronger style controllability than open-source baselines while maintaining competitive intelligibility and naturalness. Code and demos will be available at https://y61329697.github.io/DMP-TTS/.

title: VNODE: A Piecewise Continuous Volterra Neural Network
abstract: This paper introduces Volterra Neural Ordinary Differential Equations (VNODE), a piecewise continuous Volterra Neural Network that integrates nonlinear Volterra filtering with continuous-time neural ordinary differential equations for image classification. Drawing inspiration from the visual cortex, where discrete event processing is interleaved with continuous integration, VNODE alternates between discrete Volterra feature extraction and ODE-driven state evolution. This hybrid formulation captures complex patterns while requiring substantially fewer parameters than conventional deep architectures. VNODE consistently outperforms stateof-the-art models with improved computational complexity as exemplified on benchmark datasets like CIFAR-10 and Imagenet-1K.

title: Towards Data Drift Monitoring for Speech Deepfake Detection in the Context of MLOps
abstract: When being delivered in applications or services on the cloud, static speech deepfake detectors that are not updated will become vulnerable to newly created speech deepfake attacks. From the perspective of machine learning operations (MLOps), this paper tries to answer whether we can monitor new and unseen speech deepfake data that drifts away from a seen reference data set. We further ask, if drift is detected, whether we can fine-tune the detector using similarly drifted data, reduce the drift, and improve the detection performance. On a toy dataset and the large-scale MLAAD dataset, we show that the drift caused by new text-to-speech (TTS) attacks can be monitored using distances between the distributions of the new data and reference data. Furthermore, we demonstrate that fine-tuning the detector using data generated by the new TTS deepfakes can reduce the drift and the detection error rates.

title: Qudit Instead of Qubit: Certification Before Flattening with Python Synthetic Data
abstract: Critical — Qudit Instead of Qubit: Certification Before Flattening with Python Synthetic Data This article fixes a blocking failure mode by replacing the old richness-lifespan explanation with a stricter certification account. It argues that the main obstacle was not that qudit-grade structure needed to exist longer, but that it was being flattened too early by 2D shortcuts, premature public-row treatment, and binary narration. The paper then supplies a tighter 3D remedy: pre-run centered layer declaration, stored-anchor custody, conservative 2.75 handling, pre-run transition identity, Pad/Public comparison, neighboring 3D sign consensus, and corrected Python/JSON artifacts that now carry the stronger runtime law directly. The result is a more explicit and testable path for protecting a qudit-grade object from early miscertification before flatter language takes over.

title: How can large language models answer questions about a device that does not exist?
abstract: Multiple-choice questions (MCQs) are widely used to evaluate large language models (LLMs), but it remains unclear whether high performance reflects heuristic test-taking strategies or coherent internal reasoning. This distinction matters for both evaluation and interpretation of LLM capabilities. If performance is driven by heuristics, MCQs may overestimate model capability. If it instead reflects coherent internal representations, MCQ results may capture more substantive reasoning processes and depend critically on task design. To address this, we constructed a fully fictional medical imaging system (Nodjoli-X34) with no real-world referent and developed a 20-item MCQ test based solely on its internal logic. Eight LLMs were evaluated across two conditions: a standard format including questions and answer options, and an answer-only format in which question stems were removed. Across 80 independent runs, models achieved near-ceiling performance in both conditions (99.4% and 99.1% accuracy, respectively). Removal of the question stems did not reduce performance, indicating that the information required to select the correct answer was contained entirely within the structure of the answer options. When reasoning was provided (79 of 80 runs), models reconstructed a coherent internal representation of the system and applied it consistently across items. Human participants performed at chance level. These findings indicate that, under conditions of global coherence, LLMs construct and apply internal representations rather than relying on question-level heuristics. Comparison with prior work suggests that LLM reasoning strategy is adaptive: when coherence is unstable, models rely on heuristics; when coherence is the only reliable signal, they rely on it.

Comparison with prior work suggests that LLM reasoning strategy is adaptive: when coherence is unstable, models rely on heuristics; when coherence is the only reliable signal, they rely on it.

title: Target Determinability under Partial Causal Observation: A Faithful Reduction Framework
abstract: Many distributed, scientific, autonomous, and auditing systems face a structural problem: global facts are generated by causal event histories, while observers usually access only partial projections of those histories. Logs, explanations, measurements, or traces therefore do not by themselves guarantee that a target fact is determinable. This paper names this structural limitation the causal observability gap and develops a formal framework for studying target determinability under partial causal observation. An external target-determination problem is written as P = (ℋ, O, Q), where ℋ is the set of possible real histories, O is the real observation, and Q is the target fact. A faithful reduction maps such a problem to a formal triple (ℱ, Ω, D), where ℱ is a family of finite causal configurations, Ω is an observation function, and D is a formal target. Faithfulness requires preservation of histories, observations, and targets. The adequacy theorem proves that, under these conditions, Q is zero-error determinable from O if and only if D is zero-error determinable from Ω. The core mathematical criterion is quotient factorization: D is determinable from Ω exactly when D is constant on every observational equivalence class, equivalently when there exists g such that D = g ∘ Ω, or equivalently when the observation partition refines the target partition, Π_Ω ≼ Π_D. If two configurations have the same observation but different target values, no decision procedure depending only on the observation can solve the target problem with zero error; the pair itself is a publicly checkable certificate of non-determinability. The paper further develops reconstruction complexity, refinement monotonicity, finite ambiguity bounds, constrained causal evidence as conflict-edge coverage, dynamic configuration streams, approximate determinability, adversarial observation, observation composition, and privacy-observability tradeoffs. The contribution is a falsifiable and reproducible mathematical framework for target-fact determinability under partial causal observation, together with an engineering checker interface.

title: Alemetria: A Protocol for Auditing Interpretational Behavior in Large Language Models (Short Version)
abstract: This record presents a condensed English version of Alemetria, a protocol for auditing interpretational behavior in large language models (LLMs). Alemetria shifts evaluation from direct output comparison to validation of the conditions under which comparison is methodologically permissible. The protocol is organized as a structured sequence (B0-B4) and introduces a rule prohibiting calculation when interpretational comparability or stability conditions are not satisfied. The method distinguishes between substantive agreement, false consensus, divergence, evasion, interpretational suppression, and instability under reformulation. This condensed version focuses on the formal logic of the protocol. For the full methodological specification, extended empirical data, case studies, and appendices, see the Russian preprint:https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19674164

title: Entanglement Capacity from SGOC Slack Purity Slack, Rényi-2 Entropy, and the Modal Capacity Spectrum
abstract: This paper is part of the SGOC programme and it identifies the canonical capacity scalar Sc with a standard quantum-information entropy on a declared entanglement branch. For a normalised pure-state bipartition A|B, when the multiplicative slack is taken to be the reduced-state purity, epsilon_A = Tr(rho_A^2), the capacity scalar is exactly the order-2 Rényi entropy, Sc,A|B = -log epsilon_A = S2(rho_A). This is not a new scalar definition. It is a branchwise identification of the already canonical SGOC scalar with the Rényi-2 entanglement entropy of the reduced state. The note checks the standard structural tests expected of such an identification: product pure states give zero capacity entropy; local unitary changes leave the scalar invariant; tensor products add because purities multiply; and the logarithmic form is canonical once a multiplicative purity slack is required to become an additive scalar coordinate. The paper also keeps the scalar/spectrum distinction explicit. The full von Neumann entropy is recovered from the modal capacities over the Schmidt spectrum, S_vN(rho_A) = sum_i lambda_i(-log lambda_i), not from a single scalar moment alone. Thus Sc records the Rényi-2 purity channel exactly, while the complete modal list is needed for full entropic bookkeeping. Within SGOC, the result gives the capacity scalar a clean entanglement reading. It strengthens the interpretation of Sc as a common scalar interface between capacity geometry, quantum structure, entropy language, and the gravity-facing lane, including the selected tensorial gravity packet to which this note is attached. The claim boundary is deliberately narrow. The paper does not claim that one scalar reconstructs arbitrary Schmidt spectra, does not derive unrestricted quantum gravity from entanglement, and does not replace established quantum-information entropy theory. It proves an exact identification on the declared purity-slack branch and records how that identification fits the existing SGOC scalar architecture. Related SGOC papers Primal Quantum Gravity: Beyond-first-order predictive laws, the Jacobson--Schrodinger bridge via capacity geometry, and common-source zeta structure. title: BioLAMR: A Biomimetically Inspired Large Language Model Adaptation Framework for Automatic Modulation Recognition
abstract: Automatic modulation recognition (AMR) is increasingly relevant to communication-sensing front ends in robotic and human-robot collaborative systems, where reliable spectrum awareness and adaptive wireless reception are desired. However, existing methods often degrade sharply at low signal-to-noise ratios (SNRs), and large language models (LLMs) are not natively compatible with continuous I/Q signals due to the inherent modality gap. We propose BioLAMR, a GPT-2 adaptation framework for AMR inspired by the auditory system's parallel time-frequency processing and cortical hierarchy. The framework combines bio-inspired dual-domain feature extraction with parameter-efficient LLM adaptation. BioLAMR includes three components. First, a lightweight dual-domain fusion (LDDF) module extracts complementary time- and frequency-domain features and fuses them through channel and spatial attention. Second, a convolutional embedding module converts continuous I/Q signals into GPT-2-compatible sequences without discrete tokenization. Third, a hierarchical fine-tuning strategy updates only 8.9% of parameters to preserve pretrained knowledge while adapting to modulation recognition. Experiments on the RadioML2016.10a and RadioML2016.10b benchmarks show that BioLAMR achieves overall accuracies of 64.99% and 67.43%, outperforming the strongest competing method by 2.60 and 2.47 percentage points, respectively. Under low-SNR conditions, it reaches 36.78% and 38.14%, the best results among the compared methods. Ablation studies verify the contribution of each component. These results demonstrate that combining dual-domain signal modeling with parameter-efficient GPT-2 adaptation is an effective route to robust AMR in challenging wireless environments.

title: Responsible Data-Driven Learning Models for Accurate and Inclusive Diabetes Diagnosis and Prediction
abstract: Diabetes mellitus is a significant issue on the global health agenda which requires early diagnosis and dependable prognosis to minimise the adverse effects in the long run and healthcare expenditures. Most particularly, data-driven learning has proven to have high potential when it comes to enhancing clinical decision support although traditional centralized machine learning methodologies have been associated with issues of data privacy, security and low inclusiveness among various populations. This paper suggests responsible learning models based on data that facilitate the extraction of knowledge in collaboration with ensuring the confidentiality and representativeness of the data. Using the distributed learning strategies, the suggested framework enables model training of multiple sources of healthcare data without sharing data directly, therefore, promoting ethical use of data and fair participation. The models are tested on clinically relevant datasets to measure the accuracy of the diagnostic, predictive and the strengths in heterogeneous setting. The comparative analysis proves that responsible distributed learning models can outperform competitive or even better than centralized ones and preserve privacy as well as cover wider data. The results demonstrate the possibilities of responsible machine learning paradigms in favor of the correct, inclusive, and sustainable prediction and diagnosis of diabetes and its inclusion in robust and reliable digital health systems.

title: Adversarial Contrastive Retrieval-Augmented Generation
abstract: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) basically strengthens natural language generation by using large language models (LLMs) where the external knowledge is integrated to enable precise and context-aware responses. However, incorporating over-length retrieved passages substantially increases computational cost and response latency due to the quadratic complexity using transformer, especially when multiple passages are concatenated. To mitigate this issue, this paper presents a query-aware prompt compression framework that selectively preserves relevant tokens while discarding those redundant tokens. In particular, an adversarial contrastive learning is implemented to enhance the robustness of the compressed prompt against noisy or semantically similar but irrelevant passages, thereby improving the compressor’s ability to concentrate the tokens with sufficient evidence. Under the RAG setting, the proposed method assures efficient token utilization by shortening the context length and reducing the computation overhead, while the answer quality and the robustness to retrieval noise are preserved. Experimental results validate the merit of the proposed adversarial contrastive prompt compression in LLM-based natural language generation under retrieval-intensive tasks.

title: CoreAnchor-QA: Center-Anchored and Self-Improving for Question-Answer Generation
abstract: Long document question-answering (QA) data is crucial for deploying domain models, yet high-quality corpora are scarce and cross-chunk evidence is hard to align, which makes generated questions and answers drift from the main theme. To address this, we propose CoreAnchor-QA, a framework that builds semantic anchors at document and chunk levels, asks from multiple perspectives around a fixed answer, and applies a two-stage gate based on semantic consistency and judgment scores together with a failure memory to form a self-improving loop. On the People’s Daily 2024 long-news benchmark, CoreAnchor-QA outperforms the best baseline by 12.26% on AlignScore chunk-level consistency (AS-Chk) and achieves improvements of 9.9%, 20.46%, and 2.88% on UniEval naturalness, understandability, and coherence. These results indicate that the proposed method keeps themes stable and makes evidence traceable while preserving diversity, improving the usability of synthetic QA data and the reliability of downstream applications.

title: Pretrain-DPFL: Mitigating Noise Detriment in Differentially Private Federated Learning with Model Pre-Training
abstract: Differentially Private Federated Learning (DPFL) strengthens privacy protection by perturbing model gradients with noise, though at the cost of reduced accuracy. Although prior empirical studies indicate that initializing from pre-trained rather than random parameters can alleviate noise disturbance, the problem of optimally fine-tuning pre-trained models in DPFL remains unaddressed. In this paper, we propose Pretrain-DPFL, a framework that systematically evaluates three most representative fine-tuning strategies: full-tuning (FT), head-tuning (HT), and unified-tuning(UT) combining HT followed by FT. Through convergence analysis under smooth non-convex loss, we establish theoretical conditions for identifying the optimal fine-tuning strategy in Pretrain-DPFL, thereby maximizing the benefits of pre-trained models in mitigating noise disturbance. Extensive experiments across multiple datasets demonstrate Pretrain-DPFL’s superiority, achieving 25.22% higher accuracy than scratch training and outperforming the second-best baseline by 8.19%, significantly improving the privacy-utility trade-off in DPFL.

title: Cross-Attentive Adapter with Regularized Domain Adaptation for Speaker Verification
abstract: We address catastrophic forgetting (CF) in automatic speaker verification (SV) during domain adaptation from Adult English (VoxCeleb) to Child English (MyST) and Adult Chinese (CNCeleb), under the assumption of no access to VoxCeleb data. We leverage embeddings of target-data inputs extracted from the pretrained VoxCeleb model, hypothesizing that these embeddings retain source-domain knowledge without requiring source data. These target-data embeddings extracted from the pretrained VoxCeleb model are referred to as pretrained-model embeddings (PMEs). We propose a cross-attentive (CA) adapter that reduces CF by dynamically balancing information between learnable target-domain embeddings and PMEs during adaptation. We design two regularization strategies: (i) K-means–based elastic weight consolidation (K-EWC), where clustered PMEs provide pseudo labels for parameter-importance estimation, and (ii) a moment-matching (MM) loss that constrains learnable target-domain embeddings to remain close to the PME distribution. We evaluate across target data training splits of increasing duration. Results show that our approaches consistently reduce CF by not degrading performance (%EER) on the source domain regardless of target data size.

title: PersonaPlex: Voice and Role Control for Full Duplex Conversational Speech Models
abstract: Recent advances in duplex speech models have enabled natural, low-latency speech-to-speech interactions. However, existing models are restricted to a fixed role and voice, limiting their ability to support structured, role-driven real-world applications and personalized interactions. In this work, we introduce PersonaPlex, a duplex conversational speech model that incorporates hybrid system prompts, combining role conditioning with text prompts and voice cloning with speech samples. PersonaPlex is trained on a large-scale synthetic dataset of paired prompts and user-agent conversations, generated with open-source large language models (LLM) and text-to-speech (TTS) models. To evaluate role conditioning in real-world settings, we extend the Full-Duplex-Bench benchmark beyond a single assistant role to multi-role customer service scenarios. Experiments show that PersonaPlex achieves strong role-conditioned behavior, voice-conditioned speech, and natural conversational responsiveness, surpassing state-of-the-art duplex speech models and hybrid large language model-based speech systems in role adherence, speaker similarity, latency, and naturalness.

title: Advantage-Weighted Policy Learning with Adaptive Regularization for Offline Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Offline reinforcement learning aims to learn effective policies while enforcing constraints to avoid querying out-of-distribution (OOD) actions. However, both overly conservative and unconstrained methods struggle to improve learning. Therefore, we combine robust constraints with value-driven improvement to propose Advantage-Weighted Policy Learning with Adaptive Regularization (APAR). Our approach comprises two components: advantage-weighted policy learning (AWPL) and uncertainty-based adaptive regularization (UAR). AWPL uses an advantage-weighted conditional VAE as the augmented behavior policy, removing hard-threshold filtering during reconstruction, thereby avoiding coverage bias. Next, AWPL selects actions with higher advantage as regularization targets between the reconstructed actions and the original actions in the dataset, improving the policy's expressiveness. Additionally, based on observations from mixed-quality datasets, we propose UAR, which dynamically adjusts the regularization strength across different tasks and datasets, resulting in greater adaptability and robustness. Finally, APAR achieves competitive or better scores on the D4RL benchmark.

AWPL uses an advantage-weighted conditional VAE as the augmented behavior policy, removing hard-threshold filtering during reconstruction, thereby avoiding coverage bias. Next, AWPL selects actions with higher advantage as regularization targets between the reconstructed actions and the original actions in the dataset, improving the policy's expressiveness. Additionally, based on observations from mixed-quality datasets, we propose UAR, which dynamically adjusts the regularization strength across different tasks and datasets, resulting in greater adaptability and robustness. Finally, APAR achieves competitive or better scores on the D4RL benchmark.

title: HiBAR: A Hidden Backdoor Attack on LLM Recommendation Services via Multi-Turn Dialogue Manipulation
abstract: Large Language Model (LLM)-based recommendation services are typically offered by third parties in two paradigms: customized LLMs that are publicly available for fine-tuning, and LLM agents where recommendations are delivered via a black-box interface. However, these services are vulnerable to backdoor attacks, enabling malicious adversaries to steer recommendations toward specific items. Unlike traditional backdoor attacks that rely on conspicuous triggers, recommendation scenarios require triggers to be naturally initiated by the user, making conventional backdoor patterns less effective. In this paper, we propose a novel multi-turn Hidden Backdoor Attack for Recommendation services (HiBAR). HiBAR is triggered based on the textual similarity across user prompts during a conversation, allowing for stealthy and controllable activation frequency. Experimental results demonstrate that in the LLM agent scenarios, our attack achieves a 100% attack success rate (ASR) and remains highly effective against a range of existing defenses, maintaining an ASR of 97.15%. These findings underscore the urgent need for novel defense mechanisms specifically designed for multi-turn interactive recommendation services.
